docs.task: How the typed document checks treat open questions: where a question's tag length is checked, at what level, and which tests cover it.

asks: Where is a question's tag length checked?
At what level (error or warning) is it checked?

data_flow.step: The agent calls the Document tool with a research, spec or plan document containing questions.
write() parses the JSON into the typed document, then calls check(&document).
check() dispatches on the document kind and calls Issues::questions on open_questions (research, spec) or clarifying_questions (plan).
Issues::questions counts chars (not bytes) of the tag; above 12 it pushes a Warning DocIssue with element set to the question id.
Issues::done sorts issues by level, errors first, and the tool prints them. With no errors the heading is 'Warnings to review:'.
At submit time the native and harness executors call check_submit, which calls blocking(); blocking drops warnings, so a long tag never refuses a submit.

files.purpose: Holds the document checks. Issues::questions (L76-99) validates every Question list: unique ids, 2 to 4 options (error), recommended index in range (error), tag over 12 chars (warning). It is called for ResearchDoc.open_questions (L119), SpecDoc.open_questions (L166), and PlanDoc.clarifying_questions (L465). blocking (L630) keeps only IssueLevel::Error items, so check_submit (L648) never refuses a submit for a long tag.

fn error(&mut self, element: impl Into<Option<String>>, message: String)
pub fn check_submit(agent: AgentName, input: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<(), String>

files.purpose: Defines Question. The tag field carries only a doc comment, '12 characters or fewer.'; no serde or schemars constraint enforces it. The question_tests module (L281) covers display_options and answer_in_context only, with tag 't'.
symbols: pub struct Question { pub id: String, pub question: String, pub tag: String, pub options: Vec<QuestionOption>, pub recommended: usize, pub multi_select: bool }

files.purpose: The document tests. fixtures_parse_and_pass asserts check() returns no issues at all for the research, spec and plan fixtures, whose question tags are short. No test builds a tag over 12 characters. The errors() helper filters to IssueLevel::Error, so warnings are invisible to every other test here.
Research fixture. Q1 has tag 'Scope' (5 chars), line 72. The spec fixture has the same tag at line 78 of fixtures/spec.json.
write() and load_view() both call check() and return the issues (Written.issues, DocumentView.issues), so a long tag appears as a warning on every document write and in the browser view.
symbols: pub fn write(kind: DocKind, md: &Path, value: &Value) -> Result<Written, String>

files.purpose: The Document tool result. With no errors it prints 'Warnings to review:' followed by each issue line, so the agent sees the tag warning but is not forced to fix it (L133-148).

validate_submit checks submit payload shapes by deserialization only. ExploreSubmit.open_questions is a u32 count; GenerateSpecSubmit.open_questions and PlanSubmit.clarifying_questions are Vec<Question>. It has no tag length rule.
symbols: pub fn validate_submit(agent: AgentName, input: &serde_json::Value) -> Result<(), String>

next_steps: If the level or coverage should change, the spec needs a decision on warning versus error, because errors would refuse the submit call and the prompts (assets/agents/explore, generate-spec, plan) already tell agents to keep tags at 12 characters or fewer.

patterns.description: The module header of check.rs states the split: errors are broken references and rules code can decide, and they block the submit call; warnings are shown to the agent and the reader. The tag length rule is on the warning side of that split, next to 'provisional names a question that does not exist' and 'cite the page by its full URL'. The other question rules (option count, recommended index, duplicate ids) are errors.
patterns.name: Errors block the submit, warnings only inform

document.problem: A Question card's tag must be 12 characters or fewer. The only code that enforces this is one branch in Issues::questions in crates/ostra-core/src/doc/check.rs, and it raises a warning, not an error. The warning does not block the submit call. No test sets a long tag, so the check has no direct coverage.

document.title: Open question tag length check in the typed document checks

submit.findings_summary: The only tag-length check is in Issues::questions in crates/ostra-core/src/doc/check.rs (line 95). It raises a Warning when the tag has more than 12 characters. The same function is used for research and spec open_questions and for plan clarifying_questions. Option count and the recommended index in the same function are Errors. blocking() keeps only errors, so check_submit never refuses a submit for a long tag. The Document tool shows the warning under 'Warnings to review:'. No test uses a tag over 12 characters. fixtures_parse_and_pass only shows that the short 'Scope' tags in the fixtures give no issues, and the other doc tests filter to errors.
not_covered: Web console rendering and clipping of long tags
